properties.statement: Wrote a throwaway script to walk the exported design and find every property whose value NAMES a node id, then check whether that id still resolves — the read-side counterpart of the write-time guard added this session. It found nine, split by cause: some were wrong when written (a typo in a prefix) and the rest were VALID when written and broke later when the target was renamed. The second group is the whole point: no write-time check can ever reach them, because nothing was wrong at the moment of writing. Also had to hand-classify each one as a genuine dangle versus a forward reference that merely sorted later in the document, which is a distinction the design has no way to express.
